questions.question_text: A pentagon has five equal sides and five equal angles. How is it classified?

options.why: Treated having five sides as irregular even though all sides and all angles are equal.

options.text: Regular only if it has right angles
options.why: Added a right-angle condition that is not part of the definition of a regular polygon.
Missed that equality of every side and every angle supplies both required checks.

questions.solution_text:
All sides are equal and all angles are equal.
The pentagon is regular.

options.why: Checked that the sides are equal but ignored that the polygon has two different angle sizes.
Used symmetry instead of checking whether every side and every angle is equal.
Ignored the stated unequal angle sizes, which are enough to prove the polygon is irregular.

questions.solution_text:
Its sides are equal, but its angles are not all equal.
The rhombus is irregular.

questions.question_text: A rectangle has four equal angles and side lengths $9$ cm, $4$ cm, $9$ cm and $4$ cm. How is it classified?

options.why: Checked the equal angles but ignored that the sides have two different lengths.
Assumed equal right angles alone are sufficient and did not check the side lengths.
Missed that the listed unequal side lengths already prove the rectangle is irregular.

questions.solution_text:
The angles are all equal, but the side lengths are not all equal.
The rectangle is irregular.

questions.question_text: Four sides of an octagon are $3$ cm and the other four sides are $4$ cm. Which fact is enough to classify it?

options.text: It is irregular because not all sides are equal.
It is regular because opposite sides may match.
options.why: Compared selected opposite sides instead of requiring all eight side lengths to be equal.

options.text: It is regular if all its angles are equal.
options.why: Ignored that a regular polygon must satisfy equal sides as well as equal angles.

options.text: It cannot be classified without measuring every angle.
options.why: Missed that one failed condition, unequal sides, is already enough to prove irregularity.

questions.solution_text:
A regular polygon must have every side equal.
The two different side lengths prove the octagon is irregular.

questions.question_text: A hexagon has six equal side lengths. What must also be true for it to be regular?

options.text: All six angles must be equal.
It must have six right angles.
options.why: Replaced equal angles with right angles, which a regular hexagon does not have.

options.text: It must have a vertical line of symmetry.
options.why: Used one possible symmetry property instead of the defining requirement that all angles are equal.
Used a quadrilateral-style parallel-side check rather than the definition of a regular polygon.

questions.solution_text:
Regular means all sides equal **and** all angles equal.
All six angles must also be equal.

questions.question_text: Which example disproves the claim, ‘If all angles of a polygon are equal, the polygon is regular’?

options.why: A square has equal angles and equal sides, so it supports the claim instead of disproving it.
An equilateral triangle has equal sides and equal angles, so it is regular and is not a counterexample.
A regular pentagon satisfies both defining conditions and therefore cannot disprove the claim.

questions.solution_text:
A non-square rectangle has four equal angles but two different side lengths.
It is irregular, so it disproves the claim.
